subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the value of p, if the lines 3x+4y=5, 2x+3y=4, px+4y=6 are concurrent.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say which two lines you would solve first and why, and what concurrency lets you do with the third.

steps.label: Solve two of the lines
steps.margin_note: First mark. Concurrent means all three pass through ONE point. Pick the two lines with no unknown in them — that point can be found outright.
steps.memory_tip: Solve the two lines that carry no unknown.
lines: (the third line px + 4y − 6 = 0 carries the unknown p)

recall.must_convey: That the two fully-numeric lines are solved together.
accept: solve the two lines that have no unknown in them
concurrent means all three meet at one point so find it from the known pair
use cross multiplication on the two complete lines
unknown lekunda unna rendu lines solve cheyyali

steps.why: The unknown sits in only one line, so the other two fix the meeting point with no algebra in the unknown at all. Choosing the right pair is what keeps this to four marks.
common_mistakes: Trying to solve a pair that contains the unknown.

steps.label: Write the point of intersection
steps.margin_note: Second mark. State the point plainly — it is the point every one of the three lines must pass through.
steps.memory_tip: That point is where all three must pass.

recall.must_convey: That the point of intersection is written down.
accept: write down the point where the two lines meet
state the point of intersection P
the two lines meet at this point

steps.why: Naming the point separates the two halves of the question: finding it, and then using it.
common_mistakes: Writing the coordinates the wrong way round.
Leaving the point as a pair of fractions without simplifying.

steps.label: Substitute into the third line
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. Because the three are concurrent, that point lies on the third line too — so putting it in must give zero, and the one unknown drops out.
steps.memory_tip: Substituting into the third gives zero, which fixes p.
lines: Given lines are concurrent, so P(−1, 2) lies on px + 4y = 6

recall.must_convey: That the point is substituted into the third line and the unknown solved for.
accept: put the point into the third line and solve for the unknown
since the lines are concurrent the point lies on the third line as well
substitute and the unknown comes out
point ni third line lo pettesthe unknown vasthundi

steps.why: Concurrency is exactly the statement that the third line also passes through that point, so substituting is not a check — it IS the equation that determines the unknown.
common_mistakes: Substituting into one of the two lines already used, which gives 0 = 0.
Sign slip when the point has a negative coordinate.

insider_note: Solve the two complete lines first and keep the one carrying p for last. The cross-multiplication denominator comes out as 1 here, so the point (−1, 2) drops out cleanly and gives p = 2.
